claim: The liver is the largest metabolic organ of the human body and vital for blood detoxification and metabolism.
source: The liver is the largest metabolic organ of the human body and vital for blood detoxification and metabolism.
evidence: This is a statement of established biological knowledge about the liver's role and size.

claim: In the lobule, blood flows through the hepatic sinusoids from the portal vein (PV) and hepatic artery toward the central vein (CV).
source: In the lobule, the functional unit of the liver, blood flows through the hepatic sinusoids from the portal vein (PV) and hepatic artery toward the central vein (CV).
evidence: This describes the established anatomical flow pattern in liver lobules, supported by citations in the sentence.

claim: Hepatocytes take up and metabolize substances transported by the blood and secrete bile through their apical surface into the bile canaliculi (BC) network.
source: The hepatocytes take up and metabolize substances transported by the blood and secrete the bile through their apical surface into the bile canaliculi (BC) network, where it flows toward the bile duct near the PV (Boyer, 2013; Meyer et al., 2017; Treyer and Müsch, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: Hepatocytes are polarized cells with a unique organization of apical and basal plasma membrane on their surface.
source: Hepatocytes are polarized cells with a unique organization of apical and basal plasma membrane on their surface (Müsch, 2014; Treyer and Müsch, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Hepatocytes exhibit a multipolar organization with multiple apical and basal domains, in contrast to simple epithelia.
source: In contrast to simple epithelia, where the cells have a single apical surface facing the lumen of organs, hepatocytes exhibit a multipolar organization, that is, they have multiple apical and basal domains (Gissen and Arias, 2015; Müsch, 2014; Treyer and Müsch, 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The multipolar organization of hepatocytes allows them to have numerous contacts with the sinusoidal and BC networks to maximize exchange of substances.
source: Such organization allows the hepatocytes to have numerous contacts with the sinusoidal and BC networks to maximize exchange of substances.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional consequence of the multipolar organization.

claim: Sinusoidal endothelial cells and hepatocytes form a heterogeneous 3D packing of cells and labyrinths of sinusoids and BC without apparent order.
source: Sinusoidal endothelial cells and hepatocytes form a heterogeneous 3D packing of cells and labyrinths of sinusoids and BC without apparent order (Gissen and Arias, 2015; Treyer and Müsch, 2013).
evidence: This describes the apparent lack of order in liver tissue structure, supported by citations.

claim: Each hepatocyte must be in contact with both sinusoidal and BC networks, yet the networks must never intersect.
source: However, the function of sinusoidal and BC networks prompt precise design requirements: each hepatocyte must be in contact with both networks, yet the networks must never intersect.
evidence: This is an inference about the design requirements based on functional considerations.

claim: Hans Elias in 1949 pioneered the structural analysis of the mammalian liver tissue.
source: Hans Elias in 1949 pioneered the structural analysis of the mammalian liver tissue (Elias, 1949a; Elias, 1949b; Elias, 1949c; Elias and Bengelsdorf, 1952).
evidence: This is a historical claim supported by citations to Elias's work.

claim: Elias proposed that the sinusoids are separated from one another by walls of hepatocytes (one-cell-thick), forming a 'continuous system of anastomosing plates, much like the walls separating the rooms within a building'.
source: He proposed a structural model whereby the sinusoids are separated from one another by walls of hepatocytes (one-cell-thick), forming a 'continuous system of anastomosing plates, much like the walls separating the rooms within a building' (Elias, 1949b; Elias, 1949c).
evidence: This describes Elias's structural model, supported by citations to his work.

claim: Elias's analysis was hampered by the difficulties of reconstructing the 3D tissue structure, which at that time relied on stereological analysis of 2D images.
source: However, the analysis underlying the structural model was hampered by the difficulties of reconstructing the 3D tissue structure, which at that time relied on stereological analysis of 2D images (Elias, 1949b; Elias, 1949c; Elias, 1971; Elias and Bengelsdorf, 1952).
evidence: This is a historical claim about the limitations of Elias's methods, supported by citations.

claim: Mouse livers were fixed, sectioned into 100 μm serial slices, and immunostained for cell nuclei (DAPI), cell borders (Phalloidin), hepatocyte apical plasma membrane (CD13), and the extracellular matrix (ECM, fibronectin and laminin).
source: Mouse livers were fixed, sectioned into 100 μm serial slices, and immunostained for cell nuclei (DAPI), cell borders (Phalloidin), hepatocyte apical plasma membrane (CD13), and the extracellular matrix (ECM, fibronectin and laminin) to visualize the basal plasma membrane of hepatocytes facing the sinusoidal endothelial cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the experimental methods used in the study.

claim: Full slices and selected regions-of-interest comprising a whole liver lobule were imaged at low resolution to determine the position of CV and PV as landmarks.
source: Full slices and selected regions-of-interest comprising a whole liver lobule were imaged at low resolution (Figure 1A–C) to determine the position of CV and PV as landmarks, which allowed locating and re-imaging individual CV-PV-axes at high-resolution (Figure 1D, corresponding to gray box in Figure 1C).
evidence: This describes the imaging strategy used, with reference to figures showing the data.

claim: The multi-resolution imaging allowed analysis of the distribution of apical and basal surfaces of single hepatocytes, as well as sinusoidal and BC network geometry in relation to the CV-PV axis.
source: The multi-resolution imaging allowed us to analyze the distribution of apical and basal surfaces of single hepatocytes (Figure 1F), as well as sinusoidal and BC network geometry (Figure 1E) in relation to the CV-PV axis.
evidence: This describes the analytical capabilities enabled by the imaging approach, with reference to figures.

claim: Analysis of thousands individual hepatocytes revealed the full complexity of distribution of the apical, lateral and basal surfaces.
source: Analysis of thousands individual hepatocytes revealed the full complexity of distribution of the apical, lateral and basal surfaces.
evidence: This summarizes the findings from analyzing many cells.

claim: Hepatocyte polarity cannot be described by a single apico-basal polarity axis.
source: However, hepatocyte polarity cannot be described by a single apico-basal polarity axis.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the analysis of hepatocyte polarity patterns.

claim: In simple epithelia, apico-basal cell polarity can be described by a single vector pointing from the cell center to a single apical pole.
source: In simple epithelia, such as in the kidney and intestine, apico-basal cell polarity can be described by a single vector pointing from the cell center to a single apical pole (Bryant and Mostov, 2008; Marcinkevicius et al., 2009; Treyer and Müsch, 2013) (see schematic in Figure 2A).
evidence: This describes the polarity of simple epithelia, supported by citations and a figure.

claim: The distribution of apical plasma membrane in hepatocytes is characterized by two well-defined perpendicular axes (bipolar and ring axes).
source: In the case of hepatocytes, the distribution of the apical plasma membrane is in between these two extreme cases, resulting in two well-defined perpendicular axes (Figure 2D).
evidence: This describes the biaxial polarity of hepatocytes, with reference to a figure showing the data.

claim: The distribution of weights is skewed in favor of the belt-like apical surfaces.
source: The distribution of weights is skewed in favor of the belt-like apical surfaces.
evidence: This describes the statistical distribution of polarity axis weights observed in the data.

claim: Extreme cases described only by a single axis are very rare in the population of hepatocytes.
source: However, extreme cases described only by a single axis are very rare in the population of hepatocytes.
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis of hepatocyte polarity patterns.

claim: The anti-correlation between apical and basal axes of the same type corroborates the mutual repulsion between apical and basal surfaces of hepatocytes.
source: This anti-correlation corroborates the mutual repulsion between apical and basal surfaces of hepatocytes.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed correlation pattern.

claim: Only weak correlations were observed between cell shape and apical cell polarity axes, implying that these cellular features are independent to a large extent.
source: Moreover, we only observed weak correlations between cell shape and apical cell polarity axes, implying that these cellular features are independent to a large extent (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes a finding from correlation analysis, with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Local averaging of the bipolar axes revealed a spatial organization of hepatocyte polarity with a pattern oriented along lines that connect CV and PV.
source: This procedure revealed a spatial organization of hepatocyte polarity with a pattern of the bipolar axis oriented along lines that connect CV and PV.
evidence: This describes a pattern observed after local averaging of polarity axes.

claim: Belt-like apical domains are oriented to facilitate bile transport along the reference direction.
source: Consequently, belt-like apical domains are oriented to facilitate bile transport along the reference direction (see also Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an inference about the functional consequence of the observed orientation pattern.

claim: The simultaneous alignment of two axes, bipolar and ring axis, is indicative of biaxial nematic order.
source: The simultaneous alignment of two axes, bipolar and ring axis, is indicative of biaxial nematic order (Luckhurst, 2015).
evidence: This interprets the observed alignment pattern in terms of liquid crystal physics, supported by a citation.

claim: The alignment of the ring axis was significantly above the prediction from uniaxial order (p=0.014), suggesting the presence of biaxial order.
source: However, we found that the alignment of the ring axis was significantly above the prediction (Figure 3G, hatched bar; p=0.014). This suggests the presence of biaxial order, which is confirmed by a detailed mathematical characterization in terms of biaxial order parameters described in Scholich et al. (2019).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from the data analysis, with reference to a figure and citation.

claim: Cell polarity axes of hepatocytes and the anisotropy of the sinusoidal network display biaxial nematic order in the liver lobule.
source: Our analysis shows that cell polarity axes of hepatocytes and the anisotropy of the sinusoidal network display biaxial nematic order in the liver lobule.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the analysis of alignment patterns.

claim: The cross-correlations revealed a periodicity of structures along the direction perpendicular to the CV-PV axis with a characteristic length-scale of 24 μm.
source: The cross-correlations revealed a periodicity of structures along this direction with a characteristic length-scale of 24 μm.
evidence: This describes a quantitative finding from cross-correlation analysis.

claim: The periodicity approximately equals the sum of the hepatocyte and sinusoid tube diameters.
source: This periodicity approximately equals the sum of the hepatocyte and sinusoid tube diameters.
evidence: This compares the measured periodicity to known cell dimensions.

claim: No evidence of periodic structures was found in the direction of the CV-PV axis.
source: In contrast, we found no evidence of periodic structures in the direction of the CV-PV axis (see Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the absence of periodicity in one direction, with reference to a figure.

claim: Periodicity in only one direction is a hallmark of a layered structure.
source: Such periodicity in only one direction is a hallmark of a layered structure.
evidence: This interprets the observed periodicity pattern in terms of structural organization.

claim: Sinusoids, hepatocytes, and BC exhibit a layered organization, with most hepatocytes forming a single layer sandwiched between sinusoidal cells.
source: Therefore, sinusoids, hepatocytes, and BC exhibit a layered organization, with most hepatocytes forming a single layer sandwiched between sinusoidal cells, supporting earlier structural models (Elias and Bengelsdorf, 1952; Elias, 1949b; Elias, 1949c).
evidence: This is a conclusion about tissue organization, supported by the data and citations to earlier models.

claim: It has been proposed that sinusoidal endothelial cells are the main organizers by self-ordering and enforcing the position and polarity of hepatocytes.
source: It has been proposed that the sinusoidal endothelial cells are the main organizers by self-ordering and enforcing the position and, hence, the polarity of hepatocytes (Hoehme et al., 2010; Sakaguchi et al., 2008).
evidence: This describes a hypothesis from prior work, supported by citations.

claim: A candidate pathway orienting the basal surface of hepatocytes is that of the transmembrane ECM receptors Integrins.
source: A candidate pathway orienting the basal surface of hepatocytes is that of the transmembrane ECM receptors Integrins (Yu et al., 2005).
evidence: This proposes a molecular mechanism, supported by a citation.

claim: Injection of siRNAs formulated into lipid nanoparticles (LNP) provides high efficacy and specificity in silencing genes in hepatocytes of adult mice.
source: The injection of siRNAs formulated into lipid nanoparticles (LNP) provides the advantage of silencing genes with high efficacy and specificity in hepatocytes of adult mice (Bogorad et al., 2014; Zeigerer et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes a technical method, supported by citations.

claim: Integrin-β1 expression was ablated in both the lateral and basal plasma membrane of hepatocytes but not in the sinusoidal endothelial cells.
source: Using super-resolution microscopy, we verified that Integrin-β1 expression was ablated in both the lateral and basal plasma membrane of hepatocytes but not in the sinusoidal endothelial cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes an experimental verification using microscopy, with reference to a figure.

claim: Injection of siRNAs against Integrin-β1 resulted in a 90% reduction in expression in comparison with control.
source: Injection of siRNAs against Integrin-β1 resulted in a 90% reduction in expression in comparison with control (injected with LNP-formulated Luciferase siRNA), as previously described (Bogorad et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes the efficacy of the knockdown, supported by a citation.

claim: Loss of Integrin-β1 in liver parenchymal cells led to barely detectable alterations during the first 2–4 weeks.
source: Loss of Integrin-β1 in liver parenchymal cells led to barely detectable alterations during the first 2–4 weeks.
evidence: This describes the time course of phenotypic changes after knockdown.

claim: After 7 weeks of treatment with Integrin-β1-specific siRNAs, major alterations in liver tissue organization were detected.
source: However, after 7 weeks of treatment with Integrin-β1-specific but not control siRNAs, when a significant number of hepatocytes are naturally replaced (Magami et al., 2002), we detected major alterations in liver tissue organization.
evidence: This describes the phenotype observed after extended knockdown, with a citation about hepatocyte turnover.

claim: The BC network appeared disrupted and more branched (due to an increase of dead-end branches) after Integrin-β1 knockdown.
source: First, the BC network appeared disrupted and more branched (due to an increase of dead-end branches) (Figure 4A).
evidence: This describes a phenotypic change observed in the knockdown, with reference to a figure.

claim: The biaxial cell polarity of hepatocytes was not compromised after Integrin-β1 knockdown.
source: Interestingly, the biaxial cell polarity of hepatocytes was not compromised. We observed almost unchanged correlation patterns between apical and basal cell polarity axes (Figure 4B) and indistinguishable distributions of their weights (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the preservation of biaxial polarity after knockdown, with reference to figures.

claim: Hepatocyte polarity is maintained by a cell-autonomous mechanism.
source: This suggests that hepatocyte polarity is maintained by a cell-autonomous mechanism.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that biaxial polarity is preserved after knockdown.

claim: There was a significant increase in apical surface at the expense of the basal surface after Integrin-β1 knockdown.
source: On the scale of individual hepatocytes, the only change was a significant increase in apical surface at the expense of the basal surface (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes a quantitative change in membrane distribution after knockdown, with reference to a figure.

claim: The long-range order of hepatocyte cell polarity was strongly perturbed after Integrin-β1 knockdown.
source: However, the long-range order of hepatocyte cell polarity was strongly perturbed (Figure 4C, D and Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This describes the loss of long-range order after knockdown, with reference to figures.

claim: Despite the silencing of Integrin-β1 being limited to hepatocytes, the sinusoidal network was also severely disrupted.
source: Surprisingly, despite the silencing of Integrin-β1 being limited to hepatocytes at the used dosage, the sinusoidal network was also severely disrupted, with loss of its long-range organization (Figure 4A, D).
evidence: This describes an unexpected finding that sinusoids are affected despite cell-specific knockdown, with reference to figures.

claim: Hepatocytes provide instructions to sinusoidal endothelial cells.
source: This suggests that also hepatocytes provide instructions to sinusoidal endothelial cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that sinusoids are disrupted despite hepatocyte-specific knockdown.

claim: Integrin-β1 knockdown results in loss of long-range liquid-crystal order of the liver lobule and a perturbed coordination between BC and sinusoidal networks.
source: In conclusion, Integrin-β1 KD results in loss of long-range liquid-crystal order of the liver lobule and a perturbed coordination between BC and sinusoidal networks.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion from the knockdown experiments.

claim: Elias's model captured some essential features of liver architecture but could not explain the heterogeneity of cells and the amorphous appearance of the tissue.
source: Although his model captured some essential features of liver architecture, it could not explain the heterogeneity of cells and the amorphous appearance of the tissue.
evidence: This is an evaluation of the limitations of Elias's model.

claim: Hepatocytes, BC and sinusoidal networks are organized as a layered structure, with a spacing of about one hepatocyte diameter and orientation along the PV-CV axis.
source: We found that hepatocytes, BC and sinusoidal networks are organized as a layered structure, with a spacing of about one hepatocyte diameter and orientation along the PV-CV axis, consistent with Elias' model of hepatic plates.
evidence: This is a summary of the findings about layered organization.

claim: The polarity axes of individual hepatocytes are not random but display a liquid-crystal order on the scale of the lobule.
source: However, a breakthrough from our analysis was that, by using biaxial nematic tensors to describe hepatocyte polarity, we discovered that the polarity axes of individual hepatocytes are not random but display a liquid-crystal order on the scale of the lobule.
evidence: This is a key finding of the study about liquid-crystal order.

claim: The hierarchy of structural order could conceivably be explained by local rules of cell-cell communication in combination with global cues (e.g. morphogen gradients).
source: The hierarchy of structural order could conceivably be explained by local rules of cell-cell communication in combination with global cues (e.g. morphogen gradients).
evidence: This is a speculative proposal about mechanisms underlying tissue organization.

claim: Sinusoid-hepatocyte co-alignment could result from a self-organization mechanism, whereby sinusoids guide hepatocyte polarization, while hepatocytes provide instructive signals that guide sinusoidal network organization.
source: Sinusoid-hepatocyte co-alignment could result from a self-organization mechanism, whereby sinusoids guide hepatocyte polarization, while hepatocytes provide instructive signals that guide sinusoidal network organization (Figure 5C).
evidence: This proposes a bidirectional communication mechanism for tissue organization, with reference to a figure.

claim: Integrin-β1 plays a novel role in orchestrating tissue structure by coupling the anisotropy of the sinusoidal network with the orientation of hepatocyte polarity.
source: This points at a novel role of Integrin-β1 in orchestrating tissue structure by coupling the anisotropy of the sinusoidal network with the orientation of hepatocyte polarity, with boundary conditions set by the large veins.
evidence: This proposes a novel function for Integrin-β1 based on the knockdown results.

claim: In the liver, sinusoids and BC each form a single connected network.
source: In the liver, sinusoids and BC each form a single connected network.
evidence: This describes a topological property of the liver networks.

claim: The two networks (sinusoids and BC) must be spatially separated, but also contact every hepatocyte to maximize the efficiency of fluid transport in the tissue.
source: The two networks must be spatially separated, but also contact every hepatocyte to maximize the efficiency of fluid transport in the tissue.
evidence: This describes functional requirements for the network architecture.

claim: The networks are not tree-like, but highly interconnected and redundant with multiple loops and multiple contacts to each hepatocyte.
source: Furthermore, the networks are not tree-like, but highly interconnected and redundant with multiple loops and multiple contacts to each hepatocyte.
evidence: This describes the topological structure of the networks.

claim: This architecture confers robustness against local damage and failure.
source: This architecture confers robustness against local damage and failure.
evidence: This is an inference about the functional consequence of the network architecture.

claim: The structural model of liquid-crystal order provides an explanation of how cells self-organize through local interactions to achieve the particular architecture of the liver.
source: Our structural model of liquid-crystal order provides an explanation of how cells self-organize through local interactions to achieve this particular architecture, which is compatible with continuous homeostatic remodeling of the tissue.
evidence: This is a summary of the explanatory power of the liquid-crystal model.

claim: The lobule-level reference system is defined by the location of the large veins within the imaging volume in terms of flux lines of solutions of the Poisson equation.
source: The lobule-level reference system is defined by the location of the large veins within the imaging volume in terms of flux lines of solutions of the Poisson equation.
evidence: This describes the method for defining the reference field J.

claim: The Poisson equation describes diffusive transport between spatially separated sources and sinks.
source: The Poisson equation describes diffusive transport between spatially separated sources and sinks.
evidence: This is a statement of established physics knowledge.

claim: 6–9 weeks old C57BL/6JOlaHsd mice (two males and one female) were used to study liver tissue organization under normal conditions.
source: To study liver tissue organization under normal conditions, 6–9 weeks old C57BL/6JOlaHsd mice (two males and one female) were purchased from Charles River Laboratory.
evidence: This describes the experimental animals used in the study.

claim: For the knockdown experiments, eight weeks old male mice were used.
source: For the knocked-down experiments, eight weeks old male mice were purchased from the same company.
evidence: This describes the experimental animals used for knockdown studies.

claim: Integrin-β1 was knocked down in four male mice by injecting siRNA formulated into lipidoid-based nanoparticles (LNP) that primarily target hepatocytes.
source: Integrin-β1 was knocked-down in mice (four males) by injecting siRNA formulated into lipidoid-based nanoparticles (LNP) that primarily target hepatocytes.
evidence: This describes the knockdown method and sample size.

claim: An analogous treatment using siRNA against luciferase was used as control in five male mice.
source: An analogous treatment using siRNA against luciferase was used as control (five males).
evidence: This describes the control condition and sample size.

claim: All procedures were performed in compliance with German animal welfare legislation and in pathogen-free conditions.
source: All procedures were performed in compliance with German animal welfare legislation and in pathogen-free conditions in the animal facility of the MPI-CBG, Dresden, Germany.
evidence: This describes the ethical and housing conditions for the experiments.

claim: Protocols were approved by the Institutional Animal Welfare Officer.
source: Protocols were approved by the Institutional Animal Welfare Officer.
evidence: This describes the ethical approval for the experiments.

claim: Liver samples were imaged in an upright multiphoton laser-scanning microscope (Zeiss LSM 780 NLO) equipped with Gallium arsenide phosphide (GaAsp) detectors.
source: Liver samples were imaged in an upright multiphoton laser-scanning microscope (Zeiss LSM 780 NLO) equipped with Gallium arsenide phosphide (GaAsp) detectors.
evidence: This describes the imaging equipment used.

claim: Low-resolution images were taken with a 25x/0.8 Zeiss objective at 1 µm voxel size.
source: Liver slices were imaged twice at low (25x/0.8 Zeiss objective, 1 µm voxel size) and high resolution (63x/1.3 Zeiss objective, 0.3 µm voxel size), respectively.
evidence: This describes the imaging parameters for low-resolution imaging.

claim: High-resolution images were taken with a 63x/1.3 Zeiss objective at 0.3 µm voxel size.
source: Liver slices were imaged twice at low (25x/0.8 Zeiss objective, 1 µm voxel size) and high resolution (63x/1.3 Zeiss objective, 0.3 µm voxel size), respectively.
evidence: This describes the imaging parameters for high-resolution imaging.

claim: Both high- and low-resolution images were processed and segmented with the Motion Tracking software.
source: Both high- and low-resolution images were processed and segmented with the Motion Tracking software as described in Morales-Navarrete et al. (2015) and Morales-Navarrete et al. (2016).
evidence: This describes the image analysis software used, with citations.

claim: The two-dimensional (2D) super-resolved images were generated by applying the Multiple Signal Classification Algorithm for super-resolution fluorescence microscopy (MuSiCal).
source: The two-dimensional (2D) super-resolved images were generated by applying the Multiple Signal Classification Algorithm for super-resolution fluorescence microscopy (MuSiCal) (Agarwal and Macháň, 2016) to a set of 50 sequential time-lapse confocal images with 0.1 µm pixel size.
evidence: This describes the super-resolution imaging method used, with a citation.
